sources.title: Tata Communications Q2 profit rises 86% to ₹341 crore, revenue up 9.6%
sources.description:
Tata Communications on Thursday reported 86.29 per cent increase in consolidated net profit at Rs 341.03 crore for September quarter FY27.
The Mumbai-headquartered company had posted a net profit (attributable to owners of the company) of Rs 183.06 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.
Revenue from operations rose 9.6 per cent to Rs 6,687.89 crore in Q2 FY27, as against Rs 6,099.75 crore in Q2 FY26.
When compared to the previous June quarter, the profit more than doubled and revenue was up by 1.6 per cent.
Data revenue grew to Rs 5,810 crore, while digital portfolio revenue rose to Rs 3,016 crore.

sources.title: South Indian Bank Q2 result: Profit rises 21% to ₹426 cr, gross NPAs fall
sources.description:
South Indian Bank on Thursday reported a 21 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 426 crore for the second quarter ended September 30.
The Kerala-based private sector bank registered a net profit of Rs 351 crore in the September quarter of the previous fiscal year.
Its total income increased to Rs 3,264 crore in the second quarter from Rs 2,923 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal year, South Indian Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income also climbed to Rs 2,796 crore in the September quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,407 crore in the year-ago period.
On the asset quality front, gross non-performing assets (NPAs) moderated to 1.24 per cent of gross advances at the end of September 2026 against 2.93 per cent a year ago.
Similarly, net NPAs or bad loans improved to 0.09 per cent at the end of September 2026 from 0.56 per cent at the end of the same month a year earlier.

sources.title: Indian Bank Q2FY27 result: Net profit rises 15% to ₹3,462 cr, income up 21%
sources.description:
Indian Bank on Thursday reported a 15 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 3,462 crore for the second quarter ended September 30.
The Chennai-based public sector lender posted a net profit of Rs 3,018 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal.
Its total income increased to Rs 23,059 crore in the second quarter from Rs 19,077 crore a year ago, Indian Bank said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 19,106 crore in the September quarter of FY27 from Rs 16,590 crore in the year-ago period.

sources.title: Net direct tax collection grows 13% to ₹13.38 trillion till October 14
sources.description:
Net direct tax collection rose 13.21 per cent to about Rs 13.38 lakh crore between April 1 and October 14, driven by a healthy pick-up in corporate taxes.
Net corporate tax mop-up grew 20.58 per cent to over Rs 5.99 lakh crore, while non-corporate tax (paid by individuals, firms and HUFs) rose 5.83 per cent to about Rs 6.92 lakh crore so far this fiscal year.
Collection from securities transaction tax (STT) swelled 52 per cent to Rs 46,840 crore till October 14 of FY27.
Refund issuances soared 24.22 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.65 lakh crore during the period.
On a gross basis, direct tax collection rose 15 per cent to Rs 16.03 lakh crore till October 14. This included corporate tax collection of Rs 7.53 lakh crore and non-corporate tax of Rs 8.03 lakh crore.

sources.title: Nestle India Q2 result: Net profit rises 36% to ₹1,026 cr, revenue up 20%
sources.description:
FMCG major Nestle India on Thursday reported a 36.32 per cent rise in consolidated net profit at Rs 1,026.77 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis.
The company had posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 743.17 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal, Nestle India said in a regulatory filing.
Nestle India's revenue from sale of products rose 20.45 per cent to Rs 6,782.17 crore in July-September quarter of FY27. This was Rs 5,630.23 crore in the corresponding period a year ago.
"The quarter saw a continuation of strong and broad-based growth across all product groups, with total sales reaching INR 6,782.2 crore, with a growth of 20.5 per cent, which was driven by robust, double-digit volume growth," said Chairman and Managing Director Manish Tiwary.
The company continued to focus on operational efficiencies while significantly increasing investments behind its brands, with advertising and marketing spend up 46 per cent.
